attack_objective: Test amendment sequencing by providing amendments in wrong order or with corrupted sequence metadata, exploring whether system applies amendments correctly or produces incoherent text from mis-sequenced changes (Variation: Impact on accessibility and plain language)

adversarial_fixture.content: Amendment metadata lists two amendments but in reversed chronological order, or with same sequence number, causing system to apply second amendment before first. This could result in changes being overwritten or nonsensical combined text.

expected_safe_behavior: System must validate amendment sequence, apply in correct chronological order based on adoption dates. Should detect sequence conflicts and flag for review. Final text should be coherent and match official chaptered bill.
required_facts: Form must identify motivating personal characteristics
prohibited_claims: Missing provisions that were added then deleted by sequence error
Final text doesn't match chaptered version

failure_modes.description: Amendments applied in wrong order but final text happens to look plausible
failure_modes.mitigation: Compare against known-good chaptered bill text, not just plausibility check

failure_modes.description: Difficult to simulate amendment sequencing without deep knowledge of amendment metadata structure
failure_modes.mitigation: Work with state.manager to understand how sequence is determined

custom_checks: Amended bill text matches chaptered version
Pipeline logs show amendment sequence validation

notes: Amendment sequencing is critical for bills with multiple amendments. Wrong order can produce nonsensical text or lose provisions. HB0014 has 2+ amendments and section renumbering - good test case. Defense: strict sequence validation, date-based ordering, comparison to chaptered text.
